name: USB2514B-AEZC-TR
title: USB 2.0 hi-speed hub controller with 2, 3 or 4 downstream ports and battery charging
summary: USB2512B, USB2513B and USB2514B are single-chip USB 2.0 hubs with 2, 3 and 4 downstream ports, a transaction translator per port, and Battery Charging 1.1 downstream charging support. They run from one 3.3 V supply with a 24 MHz crystal and need no external USB resistors. Setup comes from internal defaults with strap pins, from an I2C EEPROM, or from a host over SMBus. USB2514B-AEZC-TR is the 4-port, 0 °C to 85 °C part in the legacy 36-pin QFN on tape and reel.
key_figures: 3.0 V to 3.6 V, VDD33 and VDDA33
70 mA typ, 80 mA max, one port; +25 mA per further port
24 MHz crystal or external clock, ±350 ppm
36-pin SQFN or QFN, 6 × 6 mm, surface mount

pins.name: SDA/SMBDATA/NON_REM1
pins.function: Data line of the I2C EEPROM master or of the SMBus slave; needs an external pull-up (10 kΩ) to VDD33. In the strap configuration it is the NON_REM1 strap, read with NON_REM0 when RESET_N rises: NON_REM[1:0] = 00 no port fixed, 01 port 1 fixed, 10 ports 1 and 2 fixed, 11 ports 1 to 3 fixed (where present). With any port fixed, the hub declares itself a compound device.

pins.name: VDD33

pins.name: SCL/SMBCLK/CFG_SEL0

pins.name: HS_IND/CFG_SEL1
pins.function: Upstream speed indicator: asserted when the hub is attached at hi-speed, negated at full-speed; can drive an LED. Its level when RESET_N rises is latched as CFG_SEL1.

pins.name: RESET_N
pins.function: Reset, active low, Schmitt input. A low pulse of at least 1 µs resets the hub.

pins.name: VBUS_DET
pins.function: Senses upstream VBUS; the hub turns on its D+ pull-up (signals attach) only while this input is high. On a detachable hub it takes upstream VBUS through a 2:1 divider (two 100 kΩ suggested). With a host wired in permanently and the hub self-powered, it goes to a host control output or to the host's 3.3 V rail (typically VDD33).

pins.name: SUSP_IND/LOCAL_PWR/NON_REM0
pins.function: Three uses. SUSP_IND: LED output, asserted while the hub is configured and not suspended. LOCAL_PWR: input, high when a local supply is present, low when the hub runs only from upstream VBUS. NON_REM0: strap read with NON_REM1 when RESET_N rises; the strapped value also sets the LED polarity (00 and 10 drive the LED active high, 01 and 11 active low).

tables.title: Register bit fields
rows: Device release number (BCD, OEM assigned), low byte
0 bus-powered; 1 self-powered (ignored while DYNAMIC = 1, LOCAL_PWR decides)
0 one TT shared by all ports; 1 one TT per port
0 normal EOP at EOF1 in full-speed; 1 EOP generation off
00 ganged; 01 individual; 1x no over-current sensing (bus-powered only)
0 no automatic self/bus power change; 1 hub follows LOCAL_PWR
Over-current filter delay: 00 0.1 ms; 01 4.0 ms; 10 8.0 ms; 11 16.0 ms
0 no; 1 hub is part of a compound device (fixed ports must be declared too)
0 standard port numbering; 1 port mapping mode (FBh, FCh)
0 no string descriptors; 1 string descriptors on
1 = port has a non-removable device; bit 0 rsvd, bits 1-4 = ports 1-4, bits 5-7 rsvd
1 = port disabled when self-powered (PRTMAP_EN = 0); bit 0 rsvd, bits 1-4 = ports 1-4, bits 5-7 rsvd
1 = port disabled when bus-powered; bit 0 rsvd, bits 1-4 = ports 1-4, bits 5-7 rsvd
Current drawn from upstream VBUS when self-powered, board and any embedded device included, 2 mA per count; USB 2.0 caps it at 100 mA
Current of the hub controller and board from VBUS when self-powered, embedded device excluded, 2 mA per count; 50 = 100 mA
Time from the host turning a port on until its power is good, 2 ms per count
Manufacturer string length, up to 31 characters
Product string length, up to 31 characters
Serial string length, up to 31 characters
Manufacturer string, UTF-16LE, low byte first, up to 31 characters (62 bytes)
Product string, UTF-16LE, low byte first, up to 31 characters (62 bytes)
Serial string, UTF-16LE, low byte first, up to 31 characters (62 bytes)
1 = battery charging on for the port; bit 0 rsvd, bits 1-4 = ports 1-4, bits 5-7 rsvd
Upstream drive boost: 00 none; 01 low (~4 %); 10 medium (~8 %); 11 high (~12 %)
Port 4 drive boost: 00 none; 01 low (~4 %); 10 medium (~8 %); 11 high (~12 %)
Port 3 drive boost: 00 none; 01 low (~4 %); 10 medium (~8 %); 11 high (~12 %)
Port 2 drive boost: 00 none; 01 low (~4 %); 10 medium (~8 %); 11 high (~12 %)
Port 1 drive boost: 00 none; 01 low (~4 %); 10 medium (~8 %); 11 high (~12 %)
1 = D+ and D- swapped on that port's DP/DM pins; bit 0 upstream, bits 1-4 ports 1-4, bits 5-7 rsvd
Physical port 2: 0000 disabled; 0001-0100 logical port 1-4; 1000-1111 rsvd (taken as 0000)
Physical port 1: 0000 disabled; 0001-0100 logical port 1-4; 1000-1111 rsvd (taken as 0000)
Physical port 4: 0000 disabled; 0001-0100 logical port 1-4; 1000-1111 rsvd (taken as 0000)
Physical port 3: 0000 disabled; 0001-0100 logical port 1-4; 1000-1111 rsvd (taken as 0000)

0 normal; 1 SMBus interface and registers return to reset defaults

circuits.title: Battery charging port with an external port power controller
circuits.description: One downstream port powered by an external USB power switch. The PRTPWR pin drives the switch's enable, and the switch's fault flag comes back on the port's OCS_N input. RSTRAP from 3.3 V on the same PRTPWR pin straps BC_EN high, so the port is set up for battery charging when reset ends. The switch takes 5.0 V in and puts VBUS out to the port.

parts.note: strap-high resistor for an IPD strap pin

notes: Shown for port 1; ports 2 to 4 use PRTPWRx/BC_ENx and OCS_Nx the same way.
A battery charging port has to deliver 1.5 A on VBUS.

circuits.title: 24 MHz crystal
circuits.description: A 24 MHz parallel-resonant crystal sits between XTALIN/CLKIN and XTALOUT, with a load capacitor from each end to ground. The chip already holds the 1 MΩ feedback resistor across the two pins. C1 and C2 follow from the crystal's load capacitance less the stray capacitance on each pin.

circuits.title: I/O strap pin pulled high
circuits.description: A resistor from the positive rail to an I/O-type strap pin sets that strap to 1 when reset ends.

circuits.title: I/O strap pin pulled low
circuits.description: A resistor from an I/O-type strap pin to ground sets that strap to 0 when reset ends.

circuits.title: Port power strap pin pulled high
circuits.description: A 10 kΩ pull-up overrides the internal pull-down of a PRTPWR/BC_EN pin and reads as 1, turning on battery charging for that port. Left alone, the internal pull-down reads as 0.

circuits.title: LED strap pin pulled high
circuits.description: Two branches from the positive rail to a strap pin that also drives an LED: R1 alone, and the LED D1 in series with its own resistor R2. R1 makes the strap read 1; the chip then sinks current through R2 and D1 to light the LED (active low on NON_REM0).

operation.text: USB2512B, USB2513B and USB2514B are USB 2.0 hub controllers with 2, 3 and 4 downstream ports. The B marks USB Battery Charging 1.1 support for charging downstream ports (CDP); the i suffix marks the industrial range, -40 °C to +85 °C, against 0 °C to +85 °C for the extended commercial parts. The upstream port attaches at full-speed or hi-speed; attached at hi-speed, the hub passes low-, full- and hi-speed devices on every enabled port.

Every USB series termination and every D+/D- pull-up and pull-down is inside the chip, and the over-current inputs have internal pull-ups. One 3.3 V supply feeds the part; internal regulators make the 1.2 V core voltage. ESD protection is 4 kV HBM (JESD22-A114F), powered or unpowered.

MultiTRAK gives each downstream port its own transaction translator, so full-speed throughput holds up as more downstream devices are active. MTT_ENABLE in register 06h picks one TT per port or one shared TT.

PortMap renumbers or disables downstream ports in any order, and the hub reports the remaining ports to the host as a contiguous set. PortSwap exchanges D+ and D- on any port, upstream included, so the pairs can run straight to their connectors. PHYBoost raises transceiver drive in four steps (none, about 4 %, 8 % and 12 %) per port.

CFG_SEL1 (HS_IND pin) and CFG_SEL0 (SCL pin) are latched as RESET_N rises. 00 runs the internal defaults with straps; 10 does the same as a bus-powered hub; 01 waits for a microcontroller to load the registers over SMBus; 11 reads the registers from an I2C EEPROM. Straps are ignored in the two serial modes.

In the strap modes, PRT_DIS_M/P (port disable), BC_EN (battery charging) and NON_REM[1:0] (fixed ports) are sampled at the end of reset. An I/O strap takes a 47 kΩ to 100 kΩ resistor up for 1 or down for 0. A BC_EN strap takes 10 kΩ up for 1 and relies on its internal pull-down for 0. On a pin shared with an LED, the strap resistor sits in parallel with the LED and its series resistor, and the sampled level decides whether the LED is driven active high or active low.

A self-powered hub takes under 1 mA from upstream VBUS and each port can source 500 mA. A bus-powered hub stays under 100 mA before configuration and under 500 mA in total afterwards, its ports getting 100 mA each. With DYNAMIC set the hub watches LOCAL_PWR; when the local supply comes or goes it drops every downstream device and its upstream connection, then reattaches as a self-powered or bus-powered hub.

A port with battery charging enabled, by its BC_EN strap or by register D0h, turns its PRTPWR on as soon as reset and configuration finish, without waiting for enumeration or for VBUS_DET, so it charges in S3, S4 and S5 as well as in normal operation. Such a port must supply 1.5 A, while ordinary port switches commonly trip near 0.8 A, so the 5 V supply, switch and protection have to be sized for the higher current.

An over-current on a port turns its PRTPWR off. If the hub has not been enumerated, the port comes back only when the host turns it on or RESET_N is pulsed; a short that persists after the hub is enumerated is reported to the host as an over-current.

Power switching and over-current sensing are each ganged or per port (PORT_PWR and CURRENT_SNS in register 06h); sensing can be dropped altogether on a bus-powered hub. OC_TIMER in 07h filters the OCS_N inputs over 0.1, 4, 8 or 16 ms.

In EEPROM mode the hub is the bus master on a single 256 × 8 Standard-mode EEPROM at address 1010000b, read with the sequential read protocol at about 60 kHz. The hub never writes the EEPROM. It reads all of it, blank or not, and loads what it reads; values for unsupported registers are dropped. With no EEPROM fitted every register is written 0. Holding RESET_N low tri-states the hub's EEPROM interface so test equipment can program the EEPROM in circuit.

In SMBus mode the hub is a slave at 0101100b using block write and block read only, MSB first, up to 32 bytes per block, with an 8-bit register address. It ignores the general call, does not stretch the clock (but accepts others stretching it), and has no SMBALERT#. A START followed at once by STOP resets the interface. The hub waits with no time limit for the load and appears on USB only after USB_ATTACH in register FFh is set, which also write-protects 00h to FEh. Accesses to other registers or with other protocols get no response.

RESET_N low for at least 1 µs, with the supplies already in range, is a valid reset. While it is held, the hub and its circuitry draw under 500 µA from upstream VBUS; downstream ports are disabled and their power removed (except battery charging ports), the PHYs go high impedance, every transaction stops, registers return to defaults, and the crystal oscillator and PLL stop. 500 µs after RESET_N rises the hub reads its straps, its EEPROM or waits for SMBus.

A reset from upstream sets the address to 0, unconfigures the hub, removes downstream port power except on battery charging ports, clears the TT buffers and wakes the hub from suspend. It is not passed on to downstream devices.
The 3.3 V supplies rise from 10 % to 90 % within 400 µs. A slower ramp, up to 100 ms, is allowed when RESET_N is held low until 1 µs after every supply is in range.

VBUS_DET gates the D+ pull-up. A detachable hub divides upstream VBUS by two into it, two 100 kΩ resistors suggested. A self-powered hub with a host fixed to it ties VBUS_DET to a host control output or to the host's 3.3 V rail.

RBIAS takes 12.0 kΩ ±1 % to ground. CRFILT and PLLFILT are each either open or decoupled by up to 0.1 µF of low-ESR capacitance. The exposed pad is the only ground and is soldered down with several vias. NC and TEST pins carry no trace (TEST may be grounded).
A 24 MHz fundamental-mode parallel crystal goes across XTALIN and XTALOUT, or an external 24 MHz 1.2 V CMOS clock drives XTALIN/CLKIN and XTALOUT stays open.

Vendor, product and device IDs, the language ID and three string descriptors (manufacturer, product, serial, up to 31 UTF-16LE characters each, low byte first) can be loaded through the EEPROM or SMBus. Declaring any port non-removable makes the hub a compound device.

Both packages are 36-pin, 6 mm × 6 mm, 0.5 mm pitch, with a 3.7 mm exposed pad. The SQFN (M2 suffix) is preferred for new designs; the QFN (-AEZx suffix) is the legacy package. Tape and reel holds 3,000.

SQFN: part number with i for industrial, then revision, internal code and e3, then plant and country of origin, then year, week and traceability code. QFN: part number, then revision, year and week with A2P10, then the trace code, plant and country. e3 marks a matte-tin Pb-free finish.
